comparison: Perfect agreement on ALPS methodology (C19-C21, C33-C37). Both evaluations find the experimental workflow well-documented and technically sound. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation (correlation between RGB channels), while peer reviewers highlight novelty and rigor of the method.

Strong agreement on core finding that pigmentation does not predict gene expression (C22, C48-C49, C51, C74). Both evaluations find this central claim well-supported by t-SNE clustering and violin plots. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, peer reviewers describe evidence as 'solid' across all three reviewers.

Agreement on weak correlation between pigmentation genes and color (C23, C52-C53, C58-C60, C73). Both evaluations accept the quantitative correlation data from Figure 3. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with emphasis on internal consistency; peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall 'no significant correlation' finding.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding time-lag hypothesis (C24, C61-C62). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of time-series data or protein measurements. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the weak correlation data but do not specifically address the temporal interpretation, suggesting it is appropriately hedged.

Agreement on clustering results distinguishing iPSC-RPE from Lonza-RPE (C39-C42, C98-C100). Both evaluations find the clustering analysis well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes visual evidence and consistency with prior work; peer reviewers accept heterogeneity findings without challenge.

Agreement on cluster-8 characterization (C43-C47). Both evaluations accept the data on marker expression. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative adult stem cell hypothesis (C47); peer reviewers do not challenge this, likely because speculation is appropriately hedged.

Agreement on Lonza-RPE differential behavior (C50, C101-C102). Both evaluations find the observation that Lonza-RPE shows pigmentation-cluster correlation well-supported. OpenEval notes developmental interpretation is speculative but reasonable; peer reviewers accept without specific concern.

Partial agreement on complement/lysosome pathway findings (C63-C71, C75). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED emphasizing honest reporting of weak correlations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting lack of discussion on biological significance and functional implications of these correlations.

Agreement on weak visual cycle gene correlations (C72-C73). Both evaluations accept these negative findings as supporting the main conclusion. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with overall findings; peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of 'no significant correlation' conclusion.

Agreement on uncertainty of functional implications (C81). Both evaluations question whether weak correlations translate to functional differences. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting lack of functional assays; peer reviewers express similar concerns about interpretation and note biological significance remains unclear.

Agreement on quality control procedures (C25-C29). Both evaluations find the iPSC-RPE characterization methods appropriate and rigorous. OpenEval emphasizes multiple orthogonal approaches; peer reviewers explicitly state 'methods are good and experiments very rigorous.'

Disagreement on in vivo relevance claims (C104-C108). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on convergent evidence from multiple experimental systems. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting lack of proper validation experiments and Reviewer 3 questioning the hypothesis foundation and noting cell transplantation is not evaluated.

Agreement on uncertainty of plasticity and functional readiness claims (C96, C103, C109). Both evaluations find these interpretations speculative. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting need for functional validation; peer reviewers express significant concerns about physiological relevance and inadequate experimental support for in vivo hypotheses.

OpenEval finds CST3-melanin correlation and biochemical interpretation (C54-C57) SUPPORTED based on established melanin biochemistry. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this specific finding is not discussed by reviewers.

Agreement on RPE heterogeneity observation (C30-C32). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as established field knowledge motivating the study. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of quality control and experimental design (C32 shared with R8).
OpenEval finds background literature on RPE biology and AMD (C1-C13) SUPPORTED as accurate field summaries. No corresponding peer review evaluation; reviewers do not assess background claims.

OpenEval finds background on RPE immunobiology and melanin biology (C76-C95) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation; reviewers do not assess background literature claims.

OpenEval finds methodological gap identification (C18) SUPPORTED as reasonable motivation for the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation; reviewers do not specifically assess this motivational claim.

Agreement on comparative analysis design (C38, C97, C99-C100). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting appropriate comparator choice and consistency with prior work. Peer reviewers accept the comparative dataset generation without challenge as part of clustering results.
